name: Necromancy
notes: Used by Necromancers. Cast as a Shoot/Spell action, 2d6 equal to or over the difficulty. Each caster starts with one spell rolled on a d12 and may learn more; a duplicate is re-rolled or its difficulty lowered by 1. Judgement call: text taken from the group's rules doc, which is already converted to d12; the doc flags Re-Animation as an open question (see its Contradictions section).

spells.name: Lifestealer
spells.text: One model within 6" suffers one wound, no save. The Necromancer gains +1 Wound for the battle, which may take him over his starting maximum. No effect on Possessed or Undead.

spells.name: Re-Animation
spells.text: One Zombie taken out of action since the Necromancer's last activation returns. Place it within 6" of the Necromancer, not in base contact with an enemy.

spells.name: Death Vision
spells.text: The Necromancer causes fear for the rest of the battle.

spells.name: Spell of Doom
spells.text: One enemy model within 12" takes a Strength test. On a fail, roll on the Injury chart for it.

spells.name: Call of Vanhel
spells.text: One Zombie or Dire Wolf within 6" of the Necromancer moves again, up to its full Movement. If it reaches base contact with an enemy it counts as charging.

spells.name: Spell of Awakening
spells.text: Always succeeds. If an enemy Hero is killed (Dead result on the Serious Injury chart after the battle), the Necromancer may raise him as a Zombie. He keeps his characteristics, weapons and armour, but no other equipment or skills. He cannot run, is a Henchman group of one, gains no experience, and follows all Zombie rules (immune to poison, causes fear).
